title: Physics-guided learning reaches a measured radio-link threshold with fewer samples
summary: A shallow physics-guided network fitted a radio-link model from received-signal-strength measurements for a fixed reconfigurable surface. In the tested setup it reached53dB with400 measurements, versus1600 for the compared CSM method. This is a setup-specific recorded-measurement validation, not a general mobile-network or energy-efficiency benefit.
ai_technology: Parametric physics-guided neural blind beamforming; P-PGNBB

source_review.scope: Original v1 front, actual learned model Methods, clinical/physical-reference evaluation and limitations

evidence.tested: A14-parameter model learned from measured surface configurations and signal strengths. A256-element surface and fixed transmitter/receiver geometry supplied the field dataset.
evidence.unknown: The comparison concerns one fixed setup and subsets of a recorded acquisition. Test prediction error was about4.38dB; noise, model mismatch and temporal variation were not separately isolated. More flexible PGNN had lower prediction error at larger budgets. Classical phase-coherence observations and perfect-CSI simulation bounds are separate from the learned result.
evidence.ai_role: The fitted physics-guided network estimates a configuration-to-signal mapping used to select surface settings, enabling the measured sample-budget comparison.
